name: Transitive closure TC(x)
description: The smallest transitive set containing x as a subset, obtained by iterating union over ω.

name: Burali-Forti paradox
description: The class Ord of all ordinals is not a set; assuming it were yields an ordinal strictly greater than every ordinal.

name: Ordinal arithmetic
description: Addition, multiplication, and exponentiation of ordinals defined by transfinite recursion; associative but non-commutative.

name: Cantor normal form
description: Every ordinal α has a unique representation α=ω^{β₁}k₁+···+ω^{βₙ}kₙ with β₁>···>βₙ and positive integers kᵢ.

name: Epsilon numbers (ε-numbers)
description: Fixed points of ordinal exponentiation, i.e. ordinals ε satisfying ω^ε=ε, with ε₀ the least such ordinal.

name: Order type
description: The unique ordinal order-isomorphic to a given well-ordered set, given by the Mostowski collapse of its ∈-relation.

name: Rank function
description: The function assigning to each set x the least ordinal α with x∈V_{α+1}, measuring its position in the cumulative hierarchy.

name: ∈-induction (Foundation induction)
description: Proving a property holds of all sets by showing it holds of x whenever it holds of all elements of x, justified by Foundation.

name: Well-founded relation
description: A binary relation R on a class such that every nonempty subset has an R-minimal element, equivalently admits no infinite R-descending chain.

name: Well-founded recursion
description: Defining a function uniquely along a set-like well-founded relation by specifying its value at x in terms of its values at R-predecessors of x.

name: Hereditarily small sets H(κ)
description: The set of all sets whose transitive closure has cardinality strictly less than κ; H(κ) models ZFC minus Power Set for regular κ.

name: Aleph function ℵ_α
description: The order-isomorphism enumerating the infinite cardinals (initial ordinals) in increasing order, with ℵ₀ the least.

name: Initial ordinal
description: An ordinal not equinumerous with any smaller ordinal; the initial ordinals are exactly the cardinal numbers.

name: Cardinal arithmetic
description: Sum, product, and exponentiation of cardinals defined via cardinality of disjoint union, Cartesian product, and function space.

name: Hessenberg's theorem (κ²=κ)
description: Every infinite cardinal κ satisfies κ·κ=κ, proved via the Gödel pairing well-ordering of κ×κ.

name: Gödel pairing function
description: A definable well-ordering of Ord×Ord whose restriction to κ×κ is a bijection onto κ for every infinite cardinal κ.

name: Cofinality cf(α)
description: The least order type (equivalently least cardinality) of an unbounded subset of a limit ordinal α.

name: Regular cardinal
description: A cardinal κ with cf(κ)=κ, i.e. not the union of fewer than κ sets each of size less than κ.

name: Singular cardinal
description: A cardinal κ with cf(κ)<κ, i.e. expressible as a union of fewer than κ smaller sets.

name: Successor cardinals are regular
description: Under AC, every successor cardinal ℵ_{α+1} is regular.

name: Continuum function
description: The cardinal exponential κ↦2^κ giving the size of the power set; 2^{ℵ₀}=𝔠 is the continuum.

name: Hausdorff formula
description: For all α,β: ℵ_{α+1}^{ℵ_β}=ℵ_α^{ℵ_β}·ℵ_{α+1}, reducing successor-cardinal exponentiation.

name: Gimel function ℷ(κ)
description: The function ℷ(κ)=κ^{cf(κ)}; all cardinal exponentiation reduces to gimel values and the continuum function.

name: Beth function ℶ_α
description: The hierarchy ℶ₀=ℵ₀, ℶ_{α+1}=2^{ℶ_α}, ℶ_λ=sup_{α<λ}ℶ_α of iterated power-set cardinals.

name: Generalized Continuum Hypothesis (GCH)
description: The assertion 2^{ℵ_α}=ℵ_{α+1} for every ordinal α, equivalently ℶ_α=ℵ_α for all α.

name: Tukey's lemma
description: Every nonempty family of finite character has a maximal element under inclusion; equivalent to the Axiom of Choice.

name: Trichotomy of cardinals
description: For any sets X,Y either |X|≤|Y| or |Y|≤|X|; this comparability of all cardinals is equivalent to AC.

name: Ideal (set-theoretic)
description: A family of subsets closed downward and under finite unions and not containing the whole set; the dual notion to a filter.

name: κ-complete filter
description: A filter closed under intersections of fewer than κ of its members.

name: Principal vs non-principal ultrafilter
description: A principal ultrafilter is the set of all supersets of a fixed point; a non-principal one contains the cofinite filter (Fréchet filter).

name: Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem
description: Every proper filter on a set (or Boolean algebra) extends to an ultrafilter; weaker than full AC.

name: Complete Boolean algebra
description: A Boolean algebra in which every subset has a least upper bound (and dually a greatest lower bound).

name: Regular open algebra RO(P)
description: The complete Boolean algebra of regular open subsets of a topological space (or separative poset), serving as its canonical Boolean completion.

name: Closed unbounded (club) set
description: A subset of a regular uncountable cardinal κ that is unbounded and closed under suprema of its bounded subsets.

name: Club filter
description: The κ-complete normal filter on a regular uncountable κ generated by the closed unbounded subsets of κ.

name: Normal filter
description: A filter on a cardinal closed under diagonal intersection △_{α<κ}C_α; for the club filter this is equivalent to closure under regressive-function fibers.

name: Intersection of clubs is club
description: The intersection of fewer than κ club subsets of a regular uncountable κ is again club, so the club sets generate a κ-complete filter.

name: Tree (set-theoretic)
description: A partially ordered set (T,<) in which the predecessors of every node are well-ordered by <.

name: Branch, level, and height of a tree
description: A branch is a maximal chain, the α-th level is the set of nodes whose predecessors have order type α, and the height is the supremum of the levels.

name: Aronszajn tree
description: A κ-tree of height κ all of whose levels have size <κ and which has no branch of length κ.

name: Existence of an Aronszajn tree
description: An ℵ₁-Aronszajn tree exists in ZFC.

name: Suslin tree
description: An ℵ₁-tree with no uncountable chain and no uncountable antichain, equivalently a ccc Aronszajn tree.

name: Suslin's problem (Suslin Hypothesis)
description: The question whether every ccc dense complete linear order without endpoints is isomorphic to ℝ; SH asserts that it is.

name: Equivalence of Suslin tree and Suslin line
description: A Suslin line exists if and only if a Suslin tree exists.

name: Kurepa tree / Kurepa's hypothesis
description: An ℵ₁-tree with countable levels and at least ℵ₂ uncountable branches; Kurepa's Hypothesis asserts one exists.

name: Special Aronszajn tree
description: An Aronszajn tree that is the union of countably many antichains, equivalently admitting an order-preserving map into ℚ.

name: Partition calculus (arrow notation)
description: The notation κ→(λ)^n_m meaning every m-coloring of the n-element subsets of κ has a homogeneous subset of order type λ.

name: Square principle □_κ (Jensen)
description: The existence of a coherent sequence ⟨C_α:α<κ⁺⟩ of clubs C_α⊆α with otp(C_α)≤κ and coherence under limit points, holding in L.

name: Club principle ♣
description: A guessing principle giving a sequence ⟨A_α⟩ of cofinal subsets A_α⊆α such that every uncountable X⊆ω₁ contains some A_α; a weakening of ◊.

name: ◊ implies CH
description: The diamond principle ◊ on ω₁ implies the Continuum Hypothesis.

name: Singular Cardinal Hypothesis (SCH)
description: The assertion that for every singular κ with 2^{cf(κ)}<κ one has κ^{cf(κ)}=κ⁺.

name: Lévy hierarchy (Σ_n/Π_n)
description: The classification of set-theoretic formulas by the number of alternations of bounded-then-unbounded quantifiers into Σ_n, Π_n, Δ_n classes.

name: Absoluteness
description: The method of showing a formula's truth is preserved between transitive models; Δ₀ formulas are absolute and Σ₁ formulas are upward absolute.

name: Elementary submodel method
description: Taking a countable elementary submodel M≺H(θ) and applying its Mostowski collapse as a core tool for combinatorial set theory.

name: Skolem functions / Skolem hull
description: Closing a set of parameters under definable Skolem witnessing functions to obtain an elementary substructure.

name: Gödel operations 𝒢₁–𝒢₁₀
description: A finite list of ten basic finitary set operations whose closure yields exactly the Σ₀-definable (rudimentary) functions used to build L.

name: Constructible well-ordering <_L
description: The canonical Σ₁-definable well-ordering of the constructible universe L obtained from the stagewise construction of the L_α.

name: AC holds in L
description: The constructible universe L satisfies the Axiom of Choice via the definable global well-ordering <_L.

name: Relative constructibility L[A]
description: The smallest inner model of ZF closed under the definable-power-set operation relativized to a predicate A.

name: Constructible closure L(A)
description: The smallest inner model of ZF containing the set A (and its transitive closure) as an element.

name: ◊ holds in L (Jensen)
description: V=L implies the diamond principle ◊_κ on every regular uncountable κ, proved via condensation.

name: □_κ holds in L (Jensen)
description: V=L implies Jensen's square principle □_κ for every uncountable cardinal κ, proved by fine-structure methods.

name: Kurepa tree exists in L
description: V=L (via ◊⁺) implies the existence of a Kurepa tree.

name: Rudimentary functions
description: The class of functions generated by the Gödel operations and closed under composition and bounded quantification, used to define the J-hierarchy.

name: Jensen J-hierarchy J_α
description: A refinement of the constructible hierarchy built by rudimentary closure, satisfying smooth condensation at every level.

name: Σ_n-projectum ρ_n
description: For a fine-structural level, the least ordinal ρ such that some Σ_n-definable (with parameters) subset of ρ is not a member of the level.

name: Fine-structural condensation
description: The principle that Σ_n-elementary submodels of J-levels collapse to J-levels, refining Gödel's condensation lemma.

name: Silver indiscernibles
description: A closed unbounded class of ordinal order-indiscernibles for L that generate L via Skolem functions; they exist iff 0# exists.

name: 0# exists implies V≠L
description: If 0# exists then every uncountable cardinal is inaccessible (indeed indiscernible) in L, so V≠L.

name: Covering lemma implies SCH
description: If 0# does not exist, Jensen's covering lemma holds and implies the Singular Cardinal Hypothesis.

name: Notion of forcing
description: A separative partial order (P,≤,𝟙) of conditions used to extend a ground model by a generic filter.

name: Dense and predense sets
description: A subset D of a forcing poset is dense if every condition has an extension in D, and predense if every condition is compatible with a member of D.

name: Compatible and incompatible conditions
description: Two conditions are compatible if they have a common extension and incompatible otherwise; an antichain is a set of pairwise incompatible conditions.

name: Rasiowa–Sikorski lemma
description: For any countable family of dense subsets of a poset there is a filter meeting every member of the family.

name: P-names
description: Hereditarily P-labeled sets that name potential elements of a forcing extension and are interpreted via a generic filter G.

name: Canonical names (x̌, Ġ)
description: The check-name x̌ denoting a ground-model set x and the name Ġ denoting the generic filter in the forcing extension.

name: Forcing relation p⊩φ
description: The relation holding when p∈P forces φ, i.e. φ is true in M[G] for every generic G containing p.

name: Definability lemma (forcing)
description: For each formula φ the forcing relation p⊩φ is definable in the ground model.

name: Truth lemma
description: For a generic G, M[G]⊨φ if and only if some condition p∈G forces φ.

name: Forcing theorem (fundamental)
description: The Definability and Truth lemmas together reduce truth in M[G] to a ground-model-definable forcing relation.

name: Ground model definability
description: The ground model M is definable, with a parameter, inside any of its set-generic extensions (Laver–Woodin).

name: Separativity / separative quotient
description: Replacing a forcing poset by its separative quotient, densely embeddable into the regular open completion / a complete Boolean algebra.

name: Cohen forcing
description: Forcing with finite partial functions Fn(I,2) to adjoin a new real (or I-many mutually generic Cohen reals).

name: Countable chain condition (ccc)
description: A forcing poset has the ccc if every antichain in it is countable.

name: ccc forcing preserves cardinals
description: A ccc forcing notion preserves all cardinals and cofinalities of the ground model.

name: Cohen forcing is ccc
description: The poset Fn(I,2) satisfies the countable chain condition, proved via the Δ-system lemma.

name: Nice names
description: Antichain-indexed names for subsets of a ground-model set, used to count the subsets appearing in a ccc extension.

name: Con(ZFC)⟹Con(ZFC+¬CH) (Cohen)
description: Forcing with Fn(ω₂×ω,2) over a model of ZFC yields a ccc extension in which 2^{ℵ₀}=ℵ₂, so ¬CH is consistent.

name: Boolean-valued universe V^B
description: The hierarchy of B-valued names with each formula assigned a truth value ‖φ‖∈B, an alternative formulation of forcing.

name: Boolean truth value ‖φ‖
description: The recursively defined element of a complete Boolean algebra B giving the degree of truth of a formula in V^B.

name: Mixing lemma
description: Given a maximal antichain {b_i} and names {ẋ_i}, there is a single name ẋ with b_i≤‖ẋ=ẋ_i‖ for all i.

name: Maximum principle (forcing)
description: If ‖∃x φ(x)‖=b in V^B then there is a name ẋ with ‖φ(ẋ)‖=b.

name: Lévy collapse Coll(ω,κ)
description: Forcing with finite (or appropriate) conditions that collapses a cardinal κ, or all cardinals below λ, to ω.

name: <κ-closed forcing
description: A forcing notion in which every descending sequence of length <κ has a lower bound.

name: <κ-closed forcing adds no new <κ-sequences
description: A <κ-closed forcing adds no new sequences of length <κ, hence preserves H_κ and all cardinals up to κ.

name: κ-cc / κ-Knaster
description: A poset is κ-cc if all its antichains have size <κ, and κ-Knaster if every κ-sized subset has a κ-sized pairwise-compatible subset.

name: κ-cc forcing preserves cardinals ≥κ
description: A κ-cc forcing notion preserves all cardinals and cofinalities greater than or equal to κ.

name: Product forcing lemma
description: G×H is P×Q-generic over M iff G is P-generic over M and H is Q-generic over M[G], and then M[G×H]=M[G][H].

name: Two-step iteration P∗Q̇
description: The forcing that first forces with P and then with a P-name Q̇ for a poset, realized by ordered pairs of conditions.

name: Martin's Axiom MA_κ
description: For every ccc poset and every family of at most κ dense sets there is a filter meeting all of them.

name: Martin's Axiom (MA)
description: The assertion that MA_κ holds for every κ<2^{ℵ₀}.

name: MA_{ℵ₀} is a theorem of ZFC
description: Martin's Axiom for countably many dense sets is provable in ZFC, being exactly the Rasiowa–Sikorski lemma.

name: Con(MA+¬CH) (Solovay–Tennenbaum)
description: A finite-support ccc iteration of length ω₂ forces MA together with 2^{ℵ₀}=ℵ₂.

name: Finite-support iteration
description: An iterated forcing construction in which conditions have finite support, used to obtain ccc-preserving limits.

name: FS iteration of ccc is ccc
description: A finite-support iteration of ccc forcing notions is itself ccc, proved via the Δ-system lemma.

name: MA_{ℵ₁} implies ¬CH
description: Martin's Axiom for ℵ₁ dense sets implies 2^{ℵ₀}>ℵ₁, refuting the Continuum Hypothesis.

name: Con(SH) (Solovay–Tennenbaum)
description: Suslin's Hypothesis is consistent with ZFC, obtained from a model of MA+¬CH which kills all Suslin trees.

name: MA and additivity of measure/category
description: Under MA_κ the union of at most κ Lebesgue-null (resp. meager) sets of reals is null (resp. meager).

name: Countable-support iteration
description: An iterated forcing construction with countable support, the standard framework for iterating proper forcings.

name: Properness preserved under CS iteration
description: Countable-support iterations of proper forcing notions are proper (Shelah).

name: Mahlo cardinal
description: A regular cardinal κ for which the set of inaccessible cardinals below κ is stationary in κ.

name: Weakly compact cardinal
description: An inaccessible cardinal κ with the tree property, equivalently satisfying κ→(κ)²₂ or Π¹₁-indescribability.

name: Tree property characterization of weak compactness
description: For an inaccessible κ, weak compactness is equivalent to the tree property and to the partition relation κ→(κ)²₂.

name: Normal measure
description: A κ-complete nonprincipal ultrafilter on a measurable cardinal κ closed under diagonal intersections; equivalently the constant function is least nontrivial in the ultrapower.

name: Ultrapower Ult(V,U)
description: Forming V^κ/U and collapsing the well-founded structure to a transitive inner model M with elementary embedding j:V→M.

name: Measurable cardinals and elementary embeddings
description: κ is measurable iff there is a nontrivial elementary embedding j:V→M into a transitive class with critical point κ.

name: Iterated ultrapowers
description: Repeatedly taking ultrapowers by images of a measure to produce a directed system of elementary embeddings and iterates.

name: Ramsey cardinal
description: A cardinal κ satisfying the partition relation κ→(κ)^{<ω}_2.

name: Erdős cardinal κ→(α)^{<ω}
description: For an ordinal α, the least cardinal κ(α) satisfying the partition relation κ→(α)^{<ω}_2.

name: Ehrenfeucht–Mostowski models
description: Building elementary submodels generated over a set of order-indiscernibles via Skolem functions, the engine producing sharps.

name: κ→(ω₁)^{<ω} implies 0# exists
description: The existence of an Erdős/Ramsey-type cardinal with κ→(ω₁)^{<ω} yields uncountably many indiscernibles for L, hence 0#.

name: Strongly compact cardinal
description: A cardinal κ such that every κ-complete filter on any set extends to a κ-complete ultrafilter.

name: Huge cardinal
description: A cardinal κ admitting an elementary embedding j:V→M with critical point κ and ^{j(κ)}M⊆M.

name: Extenders
description: Coherent systems of ultrafilters coding a (possibly strong) elementary embedding, generalizing normal measures.

name: Vopěnka's principle
description: Every proper class of first-order structures of the same type contains two members one of which elementarily embeds into the other.

name: Proper forcing
description: A forcing notion preserving stationary subsets of [λ]^ω for all λ; equivalently generic conditions exist over countable elementary submodels.

name: Cantor space 2^ω
description: The space of infinite binary sequences with the product topology, a compact perfect totally disconnected Polish space.

name: Baire space homeomorphic to the irrationals
description: The Baire space ω^ω is homeomorphic to the space of irrational reals, via continued fractions.

name: Universality of Baire space
description: Every nonempty Polish space is a continuous image of the Baire space ω^ω.

name: Tree on a set and its body [T]
description: A set of finite sequences closed under initial segments; its body [T] of infinite branches is the corresponding closed subset of the product space.

name: Well-founded tree and its rank
description: A tree with no infinite branch, to which well-founded recursion assigns an ordinal rank.

name: Borel hierarchy (Σ⁰_α,Π⁰_α,Δ⁰_α)
description: The transfinite stratification of the Borel sets of a Polish space by iterated countable unions and complements.

name: Borel codes
description: Real-number codes for Borel sets making Borel relations definable and absolute between transitive models.

name: Property of Baire
description: A set has the Baire property if it differs from an open set by a meager set; the BP sets form a σ-algebra closed under the Suslin operation.

name: Suslin operation 𝒜
description: The operation 𝒜_s A_s=⋃_f⋂_n A_{f↾n} on a Suslin scheme that generates the analytic sets from closed sets.

name: Coanalytic set Π¹₁
description: The complement of an analytic set; the first level of the projective hierarchy dual to Σ¹₁.

name: Cantor–Bendixson derivative and rank
description: The iterated removal of isolated points from a closed set, stabilizing at a countable ordinal rank and leaving the perfect kernel.

name: Perfect set property (PSP)
description: A set of reals has the PSP if it is either countable or contains a nonempty perfect subset.

name: Analytic sets have the perfect set property
description: Every uncountable analytic set contains a nonempty perfect subset.

name: Analytic sets are Lebesgue measurable
description: Every Σ¹₁ set is Lebesgue measurable.

name: Analytic sets have the Baire property
description: Every Σ¹₁ set has the property of Baire.

name: Universal analytic set
description: A single Σ¹₁ subset of (ω^ω)² that is universal for all Σ¹₁ subsets of ω^ω, witnessing Σ¹₁≠Π¹₁.

name: Π¹₁ norm / rank
description: A regular Π¹₁-norm assigning each member the ordinal rank of an associated well-founded tree, all below ω₁.

name: Σ¹₁-boundedness theorem
description: A Σ¹₁ subset of the well-founded trees has ranks bounded below ω₁.

name: Projective hierarchy (Σ¹_n,Π¹_n,Δ¹_n)
description: The hierarchy of pointclasses with Σ¹₁ the analytic sets, Π¹_n the complements, and Σ¹_{n+1} the projections of Π¹_n sets.

name: Projective hierarchy is proper
description: For each n there is a universal Σ¹_n set, and the projective hierarchy is strictly increasing.

name: Uniformization
description: Selecting for a relation R⊆X×Y a function with graph in R, with the graph required to lie in a given pointclass.

name: Σ¹₂-uniformization (Novikov–Kondô–Addison)
description: Every Σ¹₂ relation can be uniformized by a Σ¹₂ function.

name: Prewellordering property
description: A pointclass Γ has the prewellordering property if every Γ set admits a Γ-norm; Π¹₁ and Σ¹₂ have it.

name: Scale property
description: A set has a scale if there is a sequence of norms with a convergence/lower-semicontinuity property enabling uniformization.

name: Periodicity theorems (Moschovakis)
description: Under determinacy the prewellordering and scale properties propagate up the projective hierarchy in a periodic pattern.

name: Shoenfield tree
description: A tree on ω×ω₁ whose projection is a given Σ¹₂ set, reducing membership to well-foundedness and giving Shoenfield absoluteness.

name: Σ¹₂ well-ordering under V=L
description: If V=L there is a Σ¹₂ well-ordering of the reals, yielding a Δ¹₂ non-Lebesgue-measurable set.

name: Constructible reals ℝ∩L
description: The reals belonging to L, a Σ¹₂ set which under V=L equals all reals.

name: Infinite game G(A) and strategy
description: A two-player perfect-information game on ω where players alternately play naturals, I winning iff the resulting real lies in A; a strategy is a function dictating moves.

name: Determinacy of a set Det(A)
description: The property that one of the two players has a winning strategy in the game G(A).

name: Gale–Stewart theorem
description: Every open game and every closed game (on a tree) is determined.

name: Unraveling / covering technique
description: Lifting a game to an auxiliary tree on which the payoff set becomes clopen, the key device in Martin's proof of Borel determinacy.

name: AD implies all sets Lebesgue measurable
description: Under the Axiom of Determinacy every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable.

name: AD implies the Baire property for all sets
description: Under the Axiom of Determinacy every set of reals has the property of Baire, via the Banach–Mazur game.

name: AD implies perfect set property for all sets
description: Under the Axiom of Determinacy every uncountable set of reals contains a perfect subset.

name: Banach–Mazur game
description: An infinite game in which players choose decreasing basic open sets, characterizing comeagerness and the Baire property of A.

name: Analytic determinacy
description: Every analytic (Σ¹₁) game is determined; this is equivalent to the existence of sharps for all reals and follows from a measurable cardinal (Martin, Harrington).

name: Sharps and analytic determinacy equivalence
description: The existence of x# for every real x is equivalent to the determinacy of all analytic games (Harrington–Martin).

name: Homogeneously Suslin set / homogeneous tree
description: A tree carrying a coherent commuting system of countably complete measures whose projection is a homogeneously Suslin (hence determined) set.

name: Martin–Steel theorem (projective determinacy)
description: n Woodin cardinals with a measurable above imply Π¹_{n+1}-determinacy; infinitely many Woodins imply full projective determinacy.

name: PD implies regularity for all projective sets
description: Projective Determinacy implies every projective set is Lebesgue measurable, has the Baire property and the perfect set property, and projective relations can be uniformized.

name: AD equiconsistent with infinitely many Woodins
description: Con(ZF+AD) is equivalent to Con(ZFC+there are infinitely many Woodin cardinals) (Woodin).

name: Wadge reducibility / Wadge hierarchy
description: A≤_W B iff A=f^{-1}(B) for a continuous f; under determinacy the induced degrees form a nearly well-ordered hierarchy.

name: Solovay's model construction via Lévy collapse
description: Lévy-collapsing an inaccessible cardinal to ω₁ and passing to the L(ℝ) of the extension to obtain a ZF+DC model in which all sets are Lebesgue measurable, Baire, and have the PSP.

name: Inaccessible necessary for all sets Lebesgue measurable (Shelah)
description: If every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable (with DC) then ω₁ is inaccessible in L, so an inaccessible cardinal is needed for Solovay's model.
